Q1 recorded and applied. Next.

**Question:** If an import file's first line is `"id","url","title","tags"` — valid CSV that parses to the same four column names, but with quotation marks around each — should the import accept it or reject it as a wrong header line?

Why it matters: FR-006 says the first line must be "exactly `id,url,title,tags`", which reads as a raw-text comparison, but a file that has been through a spreadsheet often comes back with every field quoted. This decides whether such a file imports or fails with status 2, and it is the difference between one test case and another.

**Recommended:** Option B - It is also the simpler implementation: the whole file, header included, goes through one CSV reader pass and the first record is compared to the four names, with no separate raw-line peek. A raw-text compare needs a second read path and would reject a header that CSV considers identical.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Reject. The header must match the raw text `id,url,title,tags` byte for byte; anything else, including a quoted equivalent, is a wrong header line and fails with status 2. |
| B | Accept. The header is compared after CSV parsing, so any valid CSV encoding of the four names in that exact order is fine; wrong names, wrong order, wrong count, or a missing header still fail with status 2. |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
